questions.stem: About the skeletal system:
options: In the adult, most of the skeleton is cartilaginous
In humans it is an endoskeleton with a cartilaginous part and a bony part
questions.explanation: Most of the skeleton is cartilaginous in the fetus; in the adult only some cartilaginous structures persist. Also false: "Its study constitutes arthrology"; "Cartilage produces the blood cells".

questions.stem: Cartilage is a tissue that is:
options: Covered by periosteum on articular surfaces
questions.explanation: Cartilage is strong but elastic and devoid of vessels and nerves. The periosteum covers bone except at the articular surfaces.

questions.stem: Which of the following are made of hyaline cartilage?
options: The thyroid and cricoid cartilages of the larynx
questions.explanation: Hyaline (translucent, bluish, vitreous): articular cartilage, thyroid and cricoid cartilages, tracheobronchial tree, nasal cartilages. The meniscus is fibrocartilage; the epiglottis is elastic cartilage.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of fibrocartilage?
questions.explanation: Fibrocartilage (whitish, resistant, rich in collagen fibres): intervertebral disc, knee meniscus, acetabular labrum. Auricular cartilage is elastic; nasal cartilages are hyaline.

questions.stem: Elastic cartilage:
questions.explanation: Elastic cartilage is yellowish, rich in elastic fibres: auricle, epiglottis and small laryngeal cartilages. Articular cartilage is hyaline. Also false: "Is bluish and translucent"; "Forms the intervertebral disc".

questions.stem: A cartilage described as "whitish, resistant and rich in collagen fibres" is:
questions.explanation: Whitish + collagen = fibrocartilage. Hyaline is bluish/translucent; elastic is yellowish with elastic fibres.

questions.stem: About the bones of the skeleton:
options: Wormian bones are supernumerary bones of the foot
Supernumerary bones are found only in the vertebral column
Sesamoid bones are supernumerary bones of the skull
Their number may vary because of supernumerary bones
questions.explanation: 206 bones, with variable supernumerary bones at the extremities (sesamoid) and in the skull (Wormian), not in the spine. Also false: "Wormian bones are supernumerary bones of the foot"; "Sesamoid bones are supernumerary bones of the skull".

questions.stem: Which of the following belong to the axial skeleton?
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton is the spine, bony head, rib cage and hyoid bone. The scapula belongs to the thoracic limb (appendicular skeleton).

questions.stem: The appendicular skeleton:
options: Is formed by the bones of the thoracic and pelvic limbs
questions.explanation: The appendicular skeleton is symmetrical, attached to the axial skeleton, made of the limb bones. Hyoid and sternum (rib cage) are axial.

questions.stem: About bone classification:
options: The vertebra is a typical short bone
A long bone has one epiphysis and two diaphyses
A flat bone has a diaphysis and two epiphyses
In a long bone, length predominates over width and thickness
In a short bone the three dimensions are almost equal
questions.explanation: The vertebra is an irregular bone, which escapes the three classic types. Short bones are e.g. carpal and tarsal bones. Also false: "A long bone has one epiphysis and two diaphyses"; "A flat bone has a diaphysis and two epiphyses".

questions.stem: Match the bone with its type:
options: The scapula is a flat bone
The carpal bones are short bones
The tarsal bones are long bones
The vertebra is a flat bone
The femur is a long bone
questions.explanation: Femur = long, scapula = flat, carpal/tarsal bones = short, vertebra = irregular.

questions.stem: Which of the following are non-articular eminences?
questions.explanation: Non-articular eminences: process, tuberosity, tubercle, spine, crest. Notch and fossa are non-articular cavities.

questions.stem: Match the bony relief with its example given in the course:
questions.explanation: The obturator foramen is a foramen (non-articular cavity) and the olecranon fossa is a fossa (non-articular cavity). An articular eminence is a head, e.g. humeral head; tubercle example: infraglenoid tubercle.

questions.stem: Non-articular cavities of bone:
options: Include the crest, e.g. the iliac crest
Serve for the passage or attachment of an anatomical element
Include the process, e.g. the coracoid process
Include the trochlear notch of the ulna
Include the foramen, an opening in the bone
questions.explanation: The trochlear notch of the ulna is an articular cavity (it receives an articular eminence). Also false: "Include the crest, e.g. the iliac crest"; "Include the process, e.g. the coracoid process".

questions.stem: Bone (osseous tissue) is:
options: A specialized, dense and strong connective tissue
Formed by 3 types of bone cells in a calcified matrix
Rich in calcium phosphate and carbonate
questions.explanation: Bone is richly vascularized, not poorly.

questions.stem: Compact bone:
options: Forms the diaphysis of long bones and delimits the medullary canal
Contains interstitial lamellae between the osteons
Contains the red bone marrow of the epiphyses
questions.explanation: Compact bone = osteons + interstitial lamellae, diaphyseal, bordering the medullary canal (yellow marrow). Trabeculae and red marrow belong to epiphyseal spongy bone.

questions.stem: About spongy bone and the diploe:
options: In the skull vault, spongy bone is called the diploe
In short bones, spongy bone surrounds compact bone
The diploe is surrounded by layers of periosteum only
Spongy bone forms the diaphysis of long bones
Spongy bone is made of trabeculae delimiting small cavities
questions.explanation: In short and flat bones compact bone surrounds the spongy bone, not the reverse. Also false: "Spongy bone forms the diaphysis of long bones"; "The diploe is surrounded by layers of periosteum only".

questions.stem: The periosteum:
options: Covers the bone except at the articular surfaces
Is responsible for growth in length
Is responsible for growth in width
questions.explanation: Growth in length depends on the growth plate (epiphyseal/conjugation cartilage) at the diaphyseal-epiphyseal junction; the periosteum does growth in width and does not cover articular surfaces.

questions.stem: A child's femur grows in length thanks to:
options: The compact bone of the diaphysis
The growth plate (epiphyseal cartilage) at the diaphyseal-epiphyseal junction
questions.explanation: Length growth = growth (conjugation) plate at the diaphyseal-epiphyseal junction; width growth = periosteum.

questions.stem: About ossification and radiological exploration of the skeleton:
options: Standard radiography explores mainly traumatic pathology (fractures)
There are two types: membranous and endochondral ossification
Ossification is preceded by a calcified bony matrix
Standard radiography is the examination of choice for tumoral pathology
questions.explanation: Ossification is preceded by a cartilaginous or membranous matrix replaced by bone, hence the two ossification types. Also false: "Ossification begins at birth"; "Standard radiography is the examination of choice for tumoral pathology".
